findings.title: Subdomain-vs-subdomain branch of website_name is not tested
findings.body: The new `website_name` method in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb has three branches: exact host match, subdomain equality (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && > 2), and the parent/child fallback. The added specs cover the exact-match branch ('example.com' == 'example.com') and the parent/child branch ('example.com' vs 'forums.example.com'), but the middle `elsif` branch — for example `forum.example.com` vs `blog.example.com` (both have 3+ segments with a shared suffix like 'example.com') — has no test. This is a meaningful logic path that should be covered; without it, regressions in subdomain matching could ship unnoticed.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed three times in website_name
findings.body: The `website_name` method calls `URI(website.to_s)` three times (once for `host`, then twice more for `.path` in each reachable branch). The serializer runs per user and is invoked for user lists (e.g. user cards, directory), so this is per-request overhead on every user serialization. Parse once into a local variable and reuse `parsed_uri.host` / `parsed_uri.path`.

findings.title: website_name silently drops URL port, query, and fragment
findings.body: `website_name` returns only `URI(...).host + URI(...).path`. For a user-supplied website such as `http://example.com:8080/users/123?ref=foo#bar`, the displayed link text becomes `example.com/users/123`, losing the port, query string, and fragment. The PR title says 'show complete URL path' but the implementation never defines what 'path' includes (path-only vs full-URL). At minimum this behavior should be documented in a comment on `website_name`, and ideally the intent (e.g., always show full URL via `URI#to_s` minus scheme, or only host+path) should be made explicit and tested.
